'''John Stuart O'Neill''' (born 2 June 1979) is a British molecular and circadian biologist. O'Neill is currently a Principal Investigator at the MRC [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in [[Cambridge|Cambridge, United Kingdom]].<ref>https://www2.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/group-leaders/n-to-s/john-oneill/ ''Laboratory Website''</ref> His work focuses on the fundamental mechanisms that sustain [[circadian rhythm]]s in [[Eukaryotic Cells|eukaryotic cells]].

==Academic career==
O'Neill studied undergraduate biochemistry at [[New College, Oxford|New College]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr John O'Neill |url=https://www.joh.cam.ac.uk/dr-john-oneill |publisher=[[St John's College, Cambridge]] |access-date=18 March 2019}}</ref> He went on to join [[King's College, Cambridge|King's College]], [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite journal |author1=University of Cambridge |title=Acta: Congregation of the Regent House on 21 July 2007 |journal=[[Cambridge University Reporter]] |date=25 July 2007 |volume=137 |issue=36 |url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/cam-only/reporter/2006-07/weekly/6082/4.html |access-date=18 March 2019|author1-link=University of Cambridge }}</ref> where he undertook his [[PhD]] research at the MRC [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]], under the supervision of [[Michael Harvey Hastings|Michael Hastings]], on the subject of cAMP signalling in the [[suprachiasmatic nucleus]] of the [[hypothalamus]] (SCN).<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/science.1152506 |pmid=18487196 |pmc=2735813 |title=CAMP-Dependent Signaling as a Core Component of the Mammalian Circadian Pacemaker |journal=Science |volume=320 |issue=5878 |pages=949–53 |year=2008 |last1=O'Neill |first1=J. S |last2=Maywood |first2=E. S |last3=Chesham |first3=J. E |last4=Takahashi |first4=J. S |last5=Hastings |first5=M. H }}</ref>

For his post-doctoral research, O'Neill investigated circadian rhythms in plants and algae with [[Andrew Millar (Scientist)|Andrew Millar]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]] and then subsequently in human cells with [[Akhilesh Reddy]] at the Institute for Metabolic Science at the [[University of Cambridge]]. During this time, O'Neill contributed to a number of papers on non-transcriptional mechanisms of circadian timekeeping,<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.cub.2008.07.021 |pmid=18786386 |title=Cellular Circadian Pacemaking and the Role of Cytosolic Rhythms |journal=Current Biology |volume=18 |issue=17 |pages=R805–R815 |year=2008 |last1=Hastings |first1=Michael H |last2=Maywood |first2=Elizabeth S |last3=O'Neill |first3=John S |s2cid=10321560 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-25950-0_4 |pmid=23604476 |chapter=Cellular Mechanisms of Circadian Pacemaking: Beyond Transcriptional Loops |title=Circadian Clocks |volume=217 |issue=217 |pages=67–103 |series=Handbook of Experimental Pharmacology |year=2013 |last1=o'Neill |first1=John S |last2=Maywood |first2=Elizabeth S |last3=Hastings |first3=Michael H |isbn=978-3-642-25949-4 }}</ref> most notably a letter and an article in same edition of [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] showing that transcriptional cycles are not essential for circadian rhythms in human and algal cells,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=O'Neill|first1=John S|last2=Reddy|first2=Akhilesh B|year=2011|title=Circadian clocks in human red blood cells|journal=Nature|volume=469|issue=7331|pages=498–503|doi=10.1038/nature09702|pmc=3040566|pmid=21270888}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=O'Neill|first1=John S|last2=Van O'Neill was awarded a [[Wellcome Trust]] Career Development Fellowship in 2011 and in 2013 was recruited to become an independent group leader in the Cell Biology Division of the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology. In 2016, he was awarded an [[EMBO Young Investigator Prize]]. In collaboration with Cairn Research, O'Neill pioneered the development of the ALLIGATOR for long-term [[bioluminescence]] imaging.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.3791/56623 |pmid=29286421 |title=Flexible Measurement of Bioluminescent Reporters Using an Automated Longitudinal Luciferase Imaging Gas- and Temperature-optimized Recorder (ALLIGATOR) |journal=Journal of Visualized Experiments |issue=130 |year=2017 |last1=Crosby |first1=Priya |last2=Hoyle |first2=Nathaniel P |last3=O'Neill |first3=John S |pmc=5755584 }}</ref>

cellular timekeeping and energy balance |journal=Nature |volume=532 |issue=7599 |pages=375–9 |year=2016 |last1=Feeney |first1=Kevin A |last2=Hansen |first2=Louise L |last3=Putker |first3=Marrit |last4=Chinoy |first4=Evan D |last5=Snider |first5=Jesse A |last6=Bessman |first6=Sara C |last7=Jung |first7=Christopher M |last8=O'Neill |first8=John S |last9=Wright |first9=Kenneth P rhythms with feeding time.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crosby|first1=Priya|last2=Hamnett|first2=Ryan|last3=Putker|first3=Marrit|last4=Hoyle|first4=Nathaniel
